scope: 30-minute bounded stability validation of the already-benchmarked native gray8 C++/Metal Session; not new feature implementation.
settings: ncc_mode=2, overlap enabled, peak1, pyramid1, batch4, fine512, resident refinement and existing bounded rescue. Use unchanged native_combined formal job settings.
reason: Largest existing 512-object workload exercises higher image, candidate and GPU buffer load; combined mode stresses asynchronous ownership, not a claim it is fastest.
lifecycle: One persistent session, recreate every100calls; stream all measurements without retaining growing outputs.
checks: Every ordered final match and proposal equal to frozen formal native_combined reference
Every asynchronous batch submitted equals completed
Frame generation increments within a session and restarts after recreation
Logical coarse/fine work and retained buffer capacities remain constant
Last-fifth median currentRSS minus first-fifth median <=max(32MiB,10percent first-fifth median)
All original source, binary and input hashes unchanged before and after
performance: Record percall time, first call and setup separately; this soak is not a replacement for paired performance comparisons.
schedule: No builds, other GPU tests or profiling concurrently. Read-only source review and documentation permitted.
evidence: Keep original runner summary and stream. The existing harness has a historical10min/2min explanatory note; duration_seconds, seconds_requested and actual duration_ms govern this new30-minute run.
completion: 30minutes is the agreed stability check for this research stage. No additional24-hour gate is planned.
limitations: Fixed synthetic image with512 separated instances of one template
Not a new-image camera stream or many different templates
Does not establish unseen-scene accuracy or guarantee absence of every possible leak
